+a TaskQueue, which is a std::priority_queue whose comparator treats all
+plain v8::Tasks as equal -- so FlushTasks() pops a batch in unspecified
+order, not FIFO. When V8 posts a delayed worker task shortly before the
+platform shuts down, the StopTask queued by DelayedTaskScheduler::Stop()
+can therefore run *before* that ScheduleTask although it was pushed
+after it. StopTask cancels the armed timers and closes the async handle;
+the ScheduleTask then arms a fresh uv timer on the dying loop, uv_run()
+stays alive until it fires, and WorkerThreadsTaskRunner::Shutdown()
+blocks in uv_thread_join() for the full delay -- observed as ~10% of
+8 s (V8's memory-reducer delay) at exit in release builds once they boot
+from the Node snapshot (which shifts startup timing enough to hit the
+Mark the scheduler stopped in StopTask and drop ScheduleTasks that run
+after it, exactly as StopTask already drops the tasks whose timers were
+armed. Upstreamable; the underlying ordering issue affects every
